[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_102]]
==== REQ-EMG-102

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_CONTRACT_DIFF_REQUESTED,contract diff is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall classify each contract item change between two git refs with its semantic version impact.


NOTE: engws contract-diff <from-ref> <to-ref> [--repo DIR] [--json] reads engmod.yml and every document it names at each ref (git show ref:path, relative to the repository prefix; a ref that is empty or starts with - is refused), loads them with the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_MODEL_LOADER,model loader>> from a temporary directory (0700, files 0600), and compares the published contract items (reqlinks.PublishedItems): added, removed, changed (text, realizers) or unchanged. Impact: capability removed, capability text changed (printed as "text changed: treated as major"), assumption added, assumption text or verificationCriteria changed, or an item kind changed are major; assumption removed, capability added and changes of realizing <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> only are minor; anything else is patch. Exit 0, or 2 on a usage or IO error.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_103]]
==== REQ-EMG-103

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_RELEASE_CHECK_REQUESTED,release check is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall reject a release that pins an unreleased dependency or whose tag bump is smaller than its contract diff requires.


NOTE: engws release-check [--repo DIR] [--tag vX.Y.Z] reports dependency.unreleased_pin (error) for every engmod.yml dependency or engmod.lock.yml version that is a pre-release or pseudo-version, and contract.semver_too_small (error) when the bump of the tag (--tag, else the highest release tag at HEAD) over the previous release tag (the highest release semver tag below it among the tags merged into the released commit, git tag --merged: the nearest ancestor release) is smaller than contract-diff(previous, the tag if it exists, else HEAD) requires. In v0.x (previous and tag major 0) a minor bump is major-capable and a patch bump minor-capable, so a breaking change needs a minor bump. Without a tag or a previous release tag the semver gate is skipped with a note. Exit 0 ok, 1 findings, 2 usage or IO error.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_105]]
==== REQ-EMG-105

Where <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FEAT_SYSTEM_COMPOSITION,system composition is enabled>>, when <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report the parents and children of each <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> and roll each linked system <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> up from its realizing child <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>>.


NOTE: trace.Matrix rows carry parents (the contract items a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> realizes through realizes or a deprecated ref, qualified alias::ID on a published <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> row, none for a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> traced only by its links or derivation; stakeholder sourceRefs are not parents, D22) and children (for a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> that is the parent of reqLinks entries: each linked child item alias::CAP-* followed by its realizing <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> alias::REQ-* at the resolved version; none for a child <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>), links (id, child, evaluated <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>>, review status) and satisfiedBy. A <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> with no code or test of its own whose every link is accepted, evaluates unchanged and resolves to an item with realizing <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> that are all implemented (or all test linked) in their own repository trace is implemented (or test linked) with satisfiedBy links (decision D18: a claimed, version-mismatched or <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_BROKEN_LINK,broken link>> gives satisfiedBy links-unreviewed and does not count), linksImplemented and linksTestLinked, is counted in the summary implemented and testLinked, and is no orphan. The summary counts linksNeedReview (each link that is version-mismatched, broken or claimed, once; <<REF_IDX-DEP_DEP_LOCAL_WORKSPACE,local workspace>> links excluded), linksVersionMismatch, linksBroken, linksClaimed and unparented (local <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> that fail the upward-trace rule of <<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_090,REQ-EMG-090>> where the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> link rules apply); linksSuspect is kept as a deprecated alias of linksVersionMismatch (D23). MCP trace.matrix returns the counts, also with summaryOnly, and parents, children, links and satisfiedBy per row.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_106]]
==== REQ-EMG-106

While <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FEAT_MCP_SERVER,mcp server is enabled>>, when <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MCP_TOOL_CALL_RECEIVED,mcp tool call is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall return the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> links of the loaded <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> with their <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> and the trace of each <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> through them.


NOTE: links.list returns every reqLinks entry with id, parent, child, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>>, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> (reqlinks.EvaluateLinks at the composed pins; no content comparison, D23), review status, needsReview, local (the dependency is a workspace checkout), pinnedVersion, dependencyVersion, reviewedBy and reviewedOn. links.suspect (name kept for compatibility) returns the links that need review (version_mismatch, broken, claimed) as engws review-links --json does, composed with the workspace off (published dependencies, module cache, offline): parent text, the child item and its realizing <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> before (at the pinned version) and after (at the dependency pin), and changes (the difference in meaning by ID). links.review {linkId, by, rationale?} writes nothing (<<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.patch refuses the link file, ADR-EMG-029), composes like engws review-links --accept with the workspace off and takes reviewedOn from the server clock: it refuses an <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_ACTOR,actor>> the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> does not define, an unknown and a <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_BROKEN_LINK,broken link>> like engws review-links --accept, and returns the command engws review-links --accept LNK --by ACT --rationale ..., the link file path relative to the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> and the line patch the command writes (pinned version, status, rationale, reviewedBy, reviewedOn, a removed fingerprint). <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>>.parents {requirementId} returns realizes, parents (the realized items; sourceRefs are no upward trace, D22), sourceRefs, derived, derivedRationale, the links the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> is parent of with <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>>, status and the linked item (id, kind, text, qualified realizers) and children (each linked item then its realizers). <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>>.get adds parents, links and children. Every tool reads only the loaded <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> and the dependencies it composes, with the lock checked and the module cache reused.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_107]]
==== REQ-EMG-107

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall render the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> link tree of a using <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> and the contract items of a child <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> without disclosing the users of the child.


NOTE: A <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> with reqLinks gets an AsciiDoc chapter "<<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,Requirement>> Links": for each <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> a list item, then each link it is the parent of with its <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> (unchanged, local, or marked *VERSION MISMATCH* with the reviewed and the dependency version, *BROKEN*, *UNPUBLISHED*) and review status (accepted, or *CLAIMED*), the linked child item alias::ID with its text, and the realizing <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> alias::REQ with their trace status in the dependency (trace.DependencyRequirementStatus), or derived with its rationale, or no <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> link; and "Assumptions of Use" with each dependency assumption and the links whose <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>> covers it (*UNVERIFIED* otherwise). A <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> that publishes contract items gets "Contract Items": each published capability and assumption of use with its text, verification criteria and realizing published <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> (no fingerprint, D23). Only when the caller opts in (AsciiDocOptions.UsedBy, <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGDOC,engdoc>> --used-by; off by default, also when a workspace is found), the render resolves an active workspace (engmod.work.yml found, the workspace not off) and a sibling replacement checkout has reqLinks onto these items through a dependency on this module path, a "Used By" section (item, using <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> id, link id, parent <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>, status) is added, computed at render time by <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>>.WorkspaceLinkUsers and never written into the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>; a document rendered with it must not be committed into the child (D16). By default a child names no using system in AsciiDoc, Gemara or MCP output. link.* findings and the strict-mode trace findings <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>.no_parent, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>.unsatisfied and contract.realizer_unpublished are reported but do not stop the render (D15).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_108]]
==== REQ-EMG-108

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall ignore each workspace file and sibling checkout that another user could have written or that leaves the workspace.


NOTE: The upward search for engmod.work.yml (FindWorkspaceWith with an empty mode and ENGMOD_WORK unset) refuses a world-writable file and, where the platform has file owners, a file owned by neither the current user nor root, with an error naming ENGMOD_WORK=<path> as the way to use it anyway; an explicit path is used as given. The Used By scan (<<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>>.WorkspaceLinkUsers) reads only replacement directories inside the workspace directory (<<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>>.PathWithin) whose manifest names no path outside its own directory (the dependency confinement, <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>>.dependency_path_escape), so a crafted workspace or sibling manifest cannot make a render read files elsewhere. The upward search does not stop at a git top-level: a workspace sits above sibling repositories by design.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_109]]
==== REQ-EMG-109

Where <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FEAT_SYSTEM_COMPOSITION,system composition is enabled>>, when <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report each <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> link whose recorded fingerprint uses another canonical form than the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> writes.


NOTE: Retired by decision D23 (ADR-EMG-030): links record no fingerprint, so there is no canonical form to be outdated. A recorded pinned.fingerprint is the error <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.pinned_fingerprint_removed (<<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_118,REQ-EMG-118>>, <<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_184,REQ-EMG-184>>); link.fingerprint_outdated no longer exists.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_110]]
==== REQ-EMG-110

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall render <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> link and contract item text without AsciiDoc passthrough.


NOTE: Text in the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,Requirement>> Links, Assumptions of Use, Contract Items and Used By sections comes partly from dependency models (another repository). Every such string is whitespace-collapsed and its passthrough forms (+++...+++, ++...++, $$...$$, pass:[...] and other pass macros) are broken with {empty}, so it renders literally and cannot emit raw HTML into the document.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_111]]
==== REQ-EMG-111

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report each accepted <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> link without a resolving reviewer and review date.


NOTE: A reqLinks entry with status accepted and no reviewedBy or no reviewedOn is link.review_unrecorded (error); a reviewedBy that is not an <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_ACTOR,actor>> of the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> and a reviewedOn that is not a YYYY-MM-DD calendar date are link.review_unrecorded too, at that field. A <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_CLAIMED_LINK,claimed link>> may carry neither. engws review-links --accept writes both; the check shows only that a modeled role and a date are recorded, review of the diff shows that the role gave it.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_112]]
==== REQ-EMG-112

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report each <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> link to a capability without a parent <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>.


NOTE: A link whose child is alias::CAP-* says that the capability satisfies a local <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>, so it needs parent: link.parent_missing (error) otherwise, also when it carries <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>>. A link to an assumption of use (alias::AOU-*) may have <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>> instead of a parent.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_113]]
==== REQ-EMG-113

While <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FEAT_MCP_SERVER,mcp server is enabled>>, when <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MCP_TOOL_CALL_RECEIVED,mcp tool call is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall write an edit of one <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> entity only when the edited <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_STATE_MODEL_VALID,model is valid>>.


NOTE: <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.patch {document, id, set?: {field: value}, unset?: [field], append?: {listField: item or [items]}, remove?: {listField: value or [values]}, write?: bool} finds the one list item with that id anywhere in the document (yamledit.FindByID: top-level entities and nested ones such as <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_FLOW_STEP,flow steps>>; no match or two matches are errors), applies set, unset, append and remove in that order with line-preserving edits (yamledit.SetPath, UnsetPath, AppendPath, RemovePath: dotted field paths such as acceptedBy.statement, a missing field or intermediate mapping is added, a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_FLOW,flow>> list stays a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_FLOW,flow>> list, an object item is removed by its id, comments and every untouched line are kept), validates the whole <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> with the edited document exactly like <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.diagnose, and returns <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_VALID,valid>>, diagnostics, otherDiagnostics, parseErrors, patch (unified diff with three lines of context, git apply format) and written. The input schema is strict (additionalProperties false; field paths ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)*$; write a JSON boolean); setting or unsetting id is refused. Decision ADR-EMG-029: it is the one <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MCP_TOOL,MCP tool>> that writes, and only with write true, only a <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_VALID,valid>> result, only a manifest-listed document other than the manifest and the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> link file (whose write path is engws review-links, D14), only when every manifest document resolves inside the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> root after symlinks, only when the file did not change during the call, through an atomic replace that keeps the file mode.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_114]]
==== REQ-EMG-114

While <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FEAT_MCP_SERVER,mcp server is enabled>>, when <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MCP_TOOL_CALL_RECEIVED,mcp tool call is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall scan the same code scope as the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> check.


NOTE: The MCP code tools (coverage.strictStatus, files.forRequirement, files.forControl, files.forThreat, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.implementations, tests.*, interfaces.implementations, code.contextForTask) scan through codescan.ScanCodeScope and codescan.CodeScopeSkip, the skip function the check and the trace use (codeScanSkipper): files git does not track or would ignore (git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard), paths matching inferenceHints.exclude and directories of nested modules are left out. Before, the MCP scanner walked repoRoot with only a fixed list of skipped directories, so git-ignored build output (viewer/dist/assets/*.js) failed coverage.strictStatus while the check passed. inferenceHints.exclude accepts dir, dir/, dir/* and dir/** (each leaves the whole directory out), ./dir, a file path and a glob with * ? [...] within one path segment (*.gen.go), relative to the module root; a pattern matches a path and every ancestor directory of it. A pattern the scan cannot apply (empty, absolute, with .., ** other than a trailing /**, a malformed glob) is <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.invalid_exclude_pattern (error) at inferenceHints.exclude[i], naming the accepted forms.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_115]]
==== REQ-EMG-115

While <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FEAT_MCP_SERVER,mcp server is enabled>>, when <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MCP_TOOL_CALL_RECEIVED,mcp tool call is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall return the type of every authorable field with the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_AUTHORING,authoring>> rules.


NOTE: validate.Rules.fieldTypes (<<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.authoringContract rules) gives, per fieldSets kind and in the same order, each field as {name, type, of?}: type string, bool, int, list<string>, list<object>, object or map<string,string>, derived by reflection from the strict-decoding Go types (fieldSetTypes); of names the fieldSets kind of an object or list<object> field (<<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_FLOW_STEP,flow steps>>: flowStep; acceptedBy: acceptanceRecord; every *<<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,Evidence>> and *Artifact struct: <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>>). fieldSets stays the list of names. The field rules also <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>>: every <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_FLOW_STEP,flow step>> needs ref (<<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.missing_flow_step_ref) and step IDs are unique across all flows (<<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.duplicate_flow_step_id within a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_FLOW,flow>>, semantic.duplicate_identity across flows); threatScenario stride is one string while preconditions, exploitPath, detection and controlVerification findings are lists; <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_CATALOG,catalog>>.term_unreferenced is reported only with lintRun.mode strict and only for a term no <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> text names, whose ID no architecture, behavior, <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ACT_COMPLIANCE_ENGINEER,assurance>>, <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPLIANCE,compliance>>, views, decisions, design or aviation string contains and whose name no other authored text contains (so a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> referenced by a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_FLOW_STEP,flow step>> ref is in use); and the exclude forms of <<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_114,REQ-EMG-114>>.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_116]]
==== REQ-EMG-116

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall warn at each acceptance record that names a decision without the owner's statement.


NOTE: <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>>.acceptance_by_decision_only (warning) at acceptedBy.statement of a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>> or <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_THREAT_SCENARIO,threat scenario>> whose acceptedBy has a decisionRef but no statement. A decision can bundle an acceptance with other choices, so the owner's own words accepting this <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>> belong on the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>>; the message asks for acceptedBy.statement and for asking the owner about the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>> by name. The record stays complete (no <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>>.acceptance_unrecorded) and the Gemara policy still lists the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>> as accepted. Imported alias::ID records are skipped.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_117]]
==== REQ-EMG-117

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall warn at each <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ACT_COMPLIANCE_ENGINEER,assurance>> record whose scoring or <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_CONTROL,control>> trace disagrees with the rest of the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.


NOTE: Three warnings (validate.assuranceConsistencyDiagnostics). <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>>.severity_inconsistent at the severity of each <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_THREAT_SCENARIO,threat scenario>> whose (likelihood, impact) pair, compared case-insensitively, maps to more than one severity among the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>'s <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_THREAT_SCENARIO,threat scenarios>>; the message names the other severities and their scenarios and asks for one scoring method recorded as a decision. Only <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_THREAT_SCENARIO,threat scenarios>> carry likelihood, impact and severity together: a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>> has likelihood, impact and residualRisk but no severity, so risks are not compared. controlVerification.risk_control_unlinked at a riskRefs entry of a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_CONTROL_VERIFICATION,control verification>> that names a local <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>> whose relatedControls omit the verification's controlRef (risk-to-control trace in both directions). threat.attack_vector_missing at the attackVectorRef of a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_THREAT_SCENARIO,threat scenario>> without one when another local <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_THREAT_SCENARIO,threat scenario>> names its <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_ATTACK_VECTOR,attack vector>>. Imported alias::ID records and unknown risks (reported elsewhere) are skipped.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_119]]
==== REQ-EMG-119

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_LINK_ADD_REQUESTED,link add is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall write a claimed <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> link pinned to the dependency version after checking its parent and child.


NOTE: engws link add [--repo DIR] (--parent REQ | --evidence REQ[,REQ]) <alias::CAP-...|alias::AOU-...> [--rationale TEXT] (decision D23): the link id is LNK-<REQ>-<ALIAS> made unique; pinned.version is the dependency pin of the alias in engmod.yml; status claimed. Before writing it validates the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> with the link added (parent <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>> IDs, declared and composed alias, a capability link needs a parent) and composes with the workspace off to check the child is a published capability or assumption of use at the pinned version (an assumption needs <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>>); it refuses a link that joins the same parent and <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>> to the same child. The link is appended to the link file with every other line kept; a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> without one gets <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>/req-links.yml and documents.reqLinks in engmod.yml. Nothing is written on refusal (exit 1).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_120]]
==== REQ-EMG-120

While <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FEAT_MCP_SERVER,mcp server is enabled>>, when <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MCP_TOOL_CALL_RECEIVED,mcp tool call is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall answer a model-reading tool for the family member checkout its repo argument names.


NOTE: Retro 1104 item 1 (decision D24). The model-reading tools (<<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.diagnose, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.patch, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.list, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.entity, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.complete, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.authoringContract, trace.matrix, <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>>.resolve, links.*, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>>.*, threats.*, verification.*, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_FLOW,flow>>.detail, flows.forRequirement, graph.*, <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_GENERATION,generation>>.*, every gemara.*) list an optional repo string in their strict input schema. The engine resolves the workspace on every call with <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.FindWorkspaceWith from the server's own <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> directory (the upward search refuses a world-writable engmod.work.yml or one owned by another user; ENGMOD_WORK names one explicitly), so a server started before engws sync wrote engmod.work.yml sees it as soon as it exists. repo is relative to the workspace root (the directory of that file, or the server's own <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> directory without one) or absolute, must hold engmod.yml and must resolve inside the root after symlinks; the tool then runs on a server initialized on that engmod.yml (cached per directory, reloading its <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> per call), its output scrubbed relative to that checkout. Without repo the server answers for its own checkout. The file and code tools stay on the server's own checkout. The MCP bridge of engineering-flow computes the family root once at startup and confines calls to it; it must re-run that per call to benefit.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_121]]
==== REQ-EMG-121

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall warn at each <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> with quantitative verification criteria that only benchmarks verify.


NOTE: Retro 1104 item 6. The code scanner marks a test entry point that is a benchmark (codemap.Symbol.Benchmark: Go Benchmark* in _test.go, Rust #[bench], now also detected as a test entry point); Criterion benchmarks are plain functions and JS bench files have no test entry-point detection, so neither is classified. A <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> whose every linking test entry point, across all test files, is a benchmark has a trace row with benchmarkOnly; when its verificationCriteria contain a digit, the trace integrity check reports verification.benchmark_only (warning) at <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>>[i]: a benchmark measures but asserts nothing, so add a Test that checks the value. A Test* or Fuzz* link in any file clears it. The <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> stays test linked.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_122]]
==== REQ-EMG-122

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_STATUS_SUGGEST_REQUESTED,status suggestion is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall print the status each <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> and <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_CONTROL_VERIFICATION,control verification>> earns from the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>> of the tree.


NOTE: Retro 1104 item 7. engws status-suggest [--repo DIR] [--tree HASH] [--json] writes nothing. The tree is the working-tree hash as engineering-flow tree-hash.mjs computes it (git add -A into a temporary copy of the index, git write-tree; the real index is unchanged), or --tree. <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,Evidence>> is the trace matrix of the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> (lock check, module cache reuse) and the lines of <git top level>/.engflow/red-checks.jsonl with that tree, verdict RED, failure not build and the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> in reqs (lines without reqs are not attributed). A local <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> earns implemented when code links it (or reviewed links roll it up as implemented); verified when also a test links it that is not environment gated (Row.Gated) and not only benchmarks (Row.BenchmarkOnly) and a RED line names it, or reviewed links roll it up as implemented and test linked; else nothing. A <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_CONTROL_VERIFICATION,control verification>> earns pass when it names at least one <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> in verificationRefs and every <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> it names earns verified; a CODE-* reference is not judged and keeps the current status. The table prints current, suggested and why per row; --json the same. Exit 0, 1 on a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> or git error.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_123]]
==== REQ-EMG-123

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall name the term and the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_CATALOG,catalog>> section of each unknown term in a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> expression.


NOTE: Retro 1104 <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> findings. ears-lint reports <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_CATALOG,catalog>>.<role>_unresolved at the same span as expr.unknown_term, the role coming from the clause position (When: <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVENT,event>>, While: <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>>, the system term: system, and so on). Both diagnostics then say unknown term "<term>" in expression (or unresolved <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_CATALOG,catalog>> term "<term>") and add it to <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_CATALOG,catalog>>.<section> (or an alias of an existing entry), the section from the role (systems, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_ACTOR,actors>>, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVENT,events>>, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,states>>, features, modes, conditions, dataTerms). A diagnostic without a paired role keeps its message.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_124]]
==== REQ-EMG-124

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report a life-cycle tier decision that disagrees with the manifest lifecycle.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-031. engmod.yml lifecycle {tier (poc, prototype, mvp, product, operational; rank 1..5), bundles (foundation, safety, security; foundation always included, bundles must be written), tierDecision, raise} is required (lifecycle.missing, ADR-EMG-061 and ADR-EMG-066; CUE #ManifestLifecycle, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.ManifestLifecycle, strict decoding). tierDecision names a decision of this <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> with status accepted whose text has a Tier: line (the first counts) equal to lifecycle.tier and a Bundles: line (comma separated; required) equal to the effective bundles, read case-insensitively; otherwise lifecycle.tier_decision_mismatch (error, rank 0) at lifecycle.tierDecision names the problem (no such decision, not accepted, no Tier: line, the tier or the bundles that differ). An unknown tier or bundle of a manifest built in Go is lifecycle.invalid_tier or lifecycle.invalid_bundle (the CUE schema rejects it on load). A manifest without lifecycle is the error lifecycle.missing (<<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_162,REQ-EMG-162>>); the golden test over every example <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> (TestExamplesGolden) records each example's diagnostics and document hashes at its declared tier, and the script that compared the repository's own <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> with v0.9.0 was retired in v0.11.0.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_125]]
==== REQ-EMG-125

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report each tier-keyed diagnostic with the severity of the project tier.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-031, internal/validate/tier_policy.go. TierPolicy() is the table of tier-keyed codes with a severity per tier: D deferred (a warning with deferred true: <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>> debt, reported, never failing a check), W warning or E error, a row for the safety bundle, and requiredFrom (the first tier where it is an error). ApplyTierPolicy(bundle, diags) runs at each public entry on the merged list: ValidateBundle, GenerateAsciiDoc (before the render gate and after the trace integrity check), BuildTraceMatrixFromFiles(With), engws check and the MCP diagnose, patch, trace.matrix and <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>>.resolve answers. It sets each tier-keyed code's severity and requiredFrom, then an open POA&M defer (<<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_129,REQ-EMG-129>>), then lifecycle.raise (exact codes or family.* patterns made errors; it never lowers). Rank-0 core codes (CoreCodes(), a closed list: <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.duplicate_id, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.broken_reference, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.invalid_*, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.missing_*, code.dangling_*, <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>>.cycle, <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>>.lock_*, link.version_mismatch, link.broken, link.parent_unknown, link.parent_missing, link.child_unpublished, link.review_unrecorded, link.invalid_status, contract.realizer_unpublished, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>.realizes_unknown, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>>.acceptance_unrecorded, the structural lifecycle.* codes and aviation.ai_actor_as_credit and aviation.authority_state_unevidenced) and every code the table does not key keep their severity. Strict code linking (code.missing_trlc_link, code.invalid_trlc_link, code.scan_failed: what coverage.strictStatus reports) is W below product and E from product. It is idempotent, does not modify its input and returns the input unchanged without lifecycle. Every row is non-decreasing from poc to operational and the safety row is never lower than the base row (TestTierPolicyMonotonic). The README Life-cycle tier section holds TierPolicyMarkdown().

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_126]]
==== REQ-EMG-126

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report a composed dependency whose life-cycle tier is below or unknown to the tier of the system.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-034. With lifecycle in the composing system, each composed dependency (a <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>> subsystem resolved at its pin) is compared with its own manifest lifecycle: a child tier below the parent tier is <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>>.dependency_below_tier (tier keyed: D D W E E) unless a local <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_RISK,risk>> recorded as accepted with a complete, resolving acceptedBy names the dependency alias in its dependencies field (preferred; each entry must be an engmod.yml dependency alias, else <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.invalid_risk_dependency, error) or the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>> subsystem that composes the dependency in appliesTo (older form, still honoured); the finding names both forms, the alias first; the one finding per dependency names the alias, the child and parent tiers and the system <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> whose links point into the child, in place of a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>.unsatisfied per <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> (a linked <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> is never <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>.unsatisfied); a child without lifecycle is <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>>.dependency_tier_unknown (W at every tier; E from product with the safety bundle). A system without lifecycle gets neither. engws bump warns when the dependency at the new version declares lifecycle and the consumer pins an engine older than v0.10.0 in its .github/engmod-check go.mod (that engine rejects the key: <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>>.load_failed).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_127]]
==== REQ-EMG-127

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall apply strict <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> links from life-cycle tier mvp.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-031 amends ADR-EMG-022. The effective <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> link mode is the maximum of requirementLinks and the tier default (guided below mvp, strict from mvp): from mvp the rules <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>.no_parent, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>.unsatisfied and link.aou_unverified apply in every <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> and the tier policy makes them errors (row D D E E E); with requirementLinks: strict declared they are errors at every tier, as in v0.9.0. requirementLinks: guided at mvp or above is lifecycle.requirement_links_conflict (error, rank 0) at requirementLinks; strict at poc is allowed. EffectiveRequirementLinkMode is exported.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_128]]
==== REQ-EMG-128

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report each <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> whose status or verification falls short of the life-cycle tier.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-031. With lifecycle only: lifecycle.requirement_unapproved at <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>>[i].status for status draft or proposed (row D D W E E); lifecycle.requirement_unverified for a status other than verified, rejected or retired, unset included (D D D W E); the trace integrity check reports verification.failed at <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>>[i] when the linked test results roll up to failed (fail, blocked, partial or flaky) and verification.gated_only when every linked test is environment gated (both D D D W E); the safety bundle needs documents.aviation (lifecycle.aviation_profile_missing) and aviation.profile.softwareLevel (lifecycle.software_level_missing), both D D E E E. Imported alias::REQ <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> are skipped.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_129]]
==== REQ-EMG-129

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report a diagnostic that an open <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_POAM_ITEM,POA&M item>> of the project tier defers as a deferred warning naming the item.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-033. #POAMItem gains defers [{code, path?}]. A tier-keyed diagnostic or a warning is deferred (warning, deferred true, poamRef the item ID; an untiered error is never deferred) when a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_POAM_ITEM,POA&M item>> with milestone tier:<project tier> (case-insensitive), status other than completed and a defers entry whose code matches (exact or family.*) and whose path is empty or equal names it; another tier's item, a completed item and another path do not. lifecycle.raise overrides a deferral. A defers entry naming a rank-0 code (or a pattern covering one) is lifecycle.poam_defers_core (error, rank 0) at poamItems[i].defers[j].code, and a rank-0 diagnostic is never deferred. The engine has no clock: an overdue item is raised by engineering-flow (tier.debt_open).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_130]]
==== REQ-EMG-130

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall render the document despite errors that only the life-cycle tier raises.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-032 extends D15 (<<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_107,REQ-EMG-107>>). In a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> with lifecycle, an error whose code the tier policy keys or lifecycle.raise names (validate.RendersDespite) fails the check (HasErrors) but does not stop GenerateAsciiDoc: the document is produced for reviewers. Rank-0 codes and every other untiered error still stop the render, and link.* and the D15 trace findings keep not stopping it.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_132]]
==== REQ-EMG-132

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report each aviation <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>> record below the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>> floor of the life-cycle tier.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-035. Only with lifecycle: the load splits ValidateAviation into structural codes (references, duplicates, hashes, arithmetic, mismatches, aviation.authority.acceptance_missing; still load-fatal) and the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> and completeness codes aviation.lifecycle.missing_category, aviation.tool.incomplete_credit_assessment and aviation.derived.incomplete_safety_feedback (<<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.AviationStateCode), which <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_VALIDATION,validation>> reports as tier-keyed diagnostics; without lifecycle all stay load-fatal as in v0.9.0. With the safety bundle, aviation.state_below_tier (D D E E E) names each record below the floor of the tier on the order declared < planned < executed < reviewed < accepted < authority-accepted: none below mvp; the five plans (PSAC, SDP, SVP, SCMP, SQAP) planned at mvp and reviewed from product; executions executed from product; every record accepted at operational; from product a software level A, B or C needs a coverage record of its metric (mcdc, decision, statement). not-applicable satisfies a floor only with lifecycleData rationale (new optional field). Applicability and independence stay those of the level's objectives. aviation.authority_state_unevidenced (error, rank 0) names a record in <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> authority-accepted with no liaison entry in authorityState authority-accepted with an authorityRecord that covers it.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_133]]
==== REQ-EMG-133

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report each aviation <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ACT_COMPLIANCE_ENGINEER,assurance>> record that names an <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ACT_AI_AGENT,AI agent>> as the person holding the credit.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-035. With lifecycle and the safety bundle, aviation.ai_actor_as_credit (error, rank 0, every tier) at aviation.reviews.<id>.reviewer, aviation.independence.<id>.producer and .verifier, aviation.executions.<id>.producer and .verifier and aviation.approvals.<id>.approver when the value, trimmed and lowercased, is a registered engineering-flow agent (validate.AIAgentNames: architecture-review, classification-review, ef-experimenter, ef-implementer, ef-modeler, export-control-review, governance-review, operability-review, performance-review, quality-review, safety-review, security-review, verification-review; the init/installer.mjs reviewers and workers). The message says AI output is input to people, asks for the person who directed and accepted the output, and to record the agent as a tool with creditClaimed false. Generic words such as ai or agent are not matched: they can be part of a person's role name.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_134]]
==== REQ-EMG-134

While <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FEAT_MCP_SERVER,mcp server is enabled>>, when <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MCP_TOOL_CALL_RECEIVED,mcp tool call is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall return what a target life-cycle tier requires that the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> does not meet.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-031. engtrace --tier-gap <tier> (JSON on stdout or --out; exit 2 for an unknown tier) and MCP tier.gap {target, repo?} return TierGapReport: currentTier (empty without lifecycle), targetTier, blocking (each diagnostic of <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_VALIDATION,validation>>, <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>> and the trace that is an error with lifecycle.tier set to the target in memory and not an error now: code, requiredFrom, severityNow (warning or absent), deferredNow, poamRef, path, message; a lifecycle.tier_decision_mismatch that the in-memory tier causes is left out), byCode, aviationBelowFloor (safety bundle: the records below the target's <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>> floor with <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> and floor, <<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_132,REQ-EMG-132>>) and dependencies (each composed dependency below the target tier or without one, with alias, subsystem, module, version, tier and required). It names rule codes only; engineering-flow joins them to life-cycle objective IDs. The engine also leaves .engflow (engineering-flow's local experiment <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> and variant worktrees) out of the MCP <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REPO_INDEX,repository index>> and the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_COMPOSITION,composition>> module digest, like .git and .engmod.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_135]]
==== REQ-EMG-135

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall load each machine authored in a behavior document with its variables, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,states>>, initial <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>>, final <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,states>>, transitions and invariants.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-037. behavior.yml gains a first-class machines block: each machine has an id SM-*, an owner <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_FUNCTIONAL_UNIT,functional unit>>, variables (type Integer, Boolean or String, each with an initial value), <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,states>> that keep their STATE-* IDs (optional final true), exactly one machine-level initial, transitions TR-* with from, to and an optional on <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVENT,event>> of behavior.<<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVENT,events>>, an optional guard and an optional effect as short strings, and invariants INV-* linked to one or more REQ-* with a Boolean expression string. Strict decoding rejects unknown fields. Schema and loader land in v0.11.0 (ADR-EMG-044).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_136]]
==== REQ-EMG-136

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall parse each machine expression text into a structured expression that records the position of any syntax error.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-039. One small built-in parser reads the operators and, or, not, implies, ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, +, -, *, the assignment :=, effect lists separated by ; and the predicate in_state(STATE-ID). The result is a stored expression tree, not text. The operator table is one shared Go table used by the parser, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_VALIDATOR,validator>> and the Quint generator. A syntax error is a diagnostic at the field with the line and column. A unary minus is the operator neg. A source over 8192 bytes or nested deeper than 64 levels is a diagnostic, not a crash (ADR-EMG-045 item 38).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_137]]
==== REQ-EMG-137

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall project each loaded machine into elements of the <<REF_IDX-DO_DO_CANONICAL_SEMANTIC_MODEL,canonical semantic model>>.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-037 and ADR-EMG-040. A machine becomes a state_definition, its <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,states>> state_usage elements, its transitions transition relationships carrying triggers, guard and effect, and its invariants constraint_usage elements with a Boolean result feature, because the generated <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYSML,SysML>> binding gives constraint_usage no authorable expression property. The initial <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> and each final <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> are projected as succession relationships (machine_initial, machine_final). Stable <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> IDs are preserved, so the views need no machine-specific code; the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_SYSML_EXPORTER,SysML exporter>> renders machines with its own writer (<<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_137,REQ-EMG-137>>, ADR-EMG-045 item 18).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_138]]
==== REQ-EMG-138

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall validate each machine against the machine rules.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-039 and ADR-EMG-043. Structural errors are always errors: a machine whose initial <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> is missing or is not one of its <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,states>> (initial is a single field, so two initial <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,states>> cannot be written), a final <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> with an outgoing transition (behavior.final_state_has_transitions), a transition whose from or to is not a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> of the same machine, an on that is not a behavior <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVENT,event>>, an undeclared variable, a type mismatch, an operator not in the table, in_state naming a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> of another machine, and a duplicate <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>>, transition or invariant ID. Advisory codes follow the tier policy: behavior.machine_deadlock (a non-final <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> without outgoing transition), behavior.transition_nondeterministic (two transitions from one <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> on the same <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVENT,event>>, or both without an <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVENT,event>>, that have no guard or the same guard text), behavior.transition_no_trigger (a transition without on and without guard), behavior.invariant_unlinked (an invariant without a REQ-*).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_139]]
==== REQ-EMG-139

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall reject free-floating behavior <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,states>> with a diagnostic that names the machines block.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-038. Every <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> belongs to exactly one machine and STATE-* IDs are kept. The free-floating list and the transitions_to and triggered_by relationship types are removed in v0.11.0 (ADR-EMG-044): the loader rejects a document that still uses them, with no opt-in mode and no automatic migration; the diagnostic message names machines: and the owner rewrites the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> by hand. The own <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>/behavior.yml of this repository is rewritten to machines (<<REF_IDX-MACHINE_SM_MODEL_VALIDATION,SM-MODEL-VALIDATION>>, <<REF_IDX-MACHINE_SM_ARTIFACT_FRESHNESS,SM-ARTIFACT-FRESHNESS>>, <<REF_IDX-MACHINE_SM_LINK_LIFECYCLE,SM-LINK-LIFECYCLE>>).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_140]]
==== REQ-EMG-140

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report each advisory machine diagnostic with the severity of the project life-cycle tier.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-043 (OWNER decision). behavior.machine_deadlock, behavior.transition_nondeterministic, behavior.transition_no_trigger and behavior.invariant_unlinked are keyed in TierPolicy with the hygiene row DDWWE: deferred at poc and prototype (a warning with the deferred flag, the off of the owner decision), warning at mvp and product, error at operational. Structural machine errors (<<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_138,REQ-EMG-138>>) are never keyed and stay errors at every tier. The Quint <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> by tier of ADR-EMG-043 (mvp: the generated modules are fresh; product: <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGQUINT,engquint>> check in run mode when machines exist; operational: verify mode for machines in safety or mission flows) are enforced by the gate steps of engineering-flow, not by the engine; this repository CI runs both modes for every <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> with machines whatever the tier (ADR-EMG-045 item 26).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_141]]
==== REQ-EMG-141

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall generate one deterministic Quint module for each machine.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-040. One .qnt module per machine, byte-identical for the same <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>. The first line is the comment Generated by engineering-model-go from <machine ID>; do not edit. Variables are prefixed v_ and IDs are sanitised to snake_case for identifiers only; a lastTransition str variable carries the TR-* ID of the last step; every variable is assigned in every action, with explicit unchanged assignments; each invariant is a val named inv_ plus the snake case of its INV-* ID (the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> it protects are named in a comment, and there is no combined inv_all); each <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> gets a reachability witness wit_<<<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>>>. Guards, effects and invariants are rendered from the expression trees with the shared operator table. New package internal/export/quint, root facade api_quint.go.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_142]]
==== REQ-EMG-142

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall generate Quint modules with <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGQUINT,engquint>> generate and check them with <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGQUINT,engquint>> check, exiting 0 on pass, 1 on a violation, a stale or drifted module or a vacuous trace and 2 on a setup error.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-040 and ADR-EMG-041. cmd/<<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGQUINT,engquint>> has the subcommands generate and check. The output directory is a CLI flag: manifest.cue has no generator-output configuration, and generated/quint/ is the path the scripts use. A setup error (missing quint, a version that cannot be read, missing Apalache or Java in verify mode, an unreadable <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>; the pinned quint version is enforced by scripts/install-quint-toolchain.sh) exits 2 and never counts as a pass.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_143]]
==== REQ-EMG-143

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall run Quint on the TypeScript backend once for each invariant.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-040 and ADR-EMG-041. quint run --backend=typescript is mandatory: the default Rust backend downloads its binary at run time. One quint run per invariant, with --max-steps, --max-samples, --seed, --invariant and --witnesses, so a violation names one invariant. A trace of length zero (an unsatisfiable initial <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>>) is an error, not a pass, because it checks nothing; a trace of length one (no transition is enabled in the initial <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>>) is a deadlock warning. One witnesses run per machine reports the reachability of each <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>>; the initial <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>> is never reported as unreachable. The counterexample <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,states>> carry lastTransition, so the report lists the TR-* IDs in order.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_144]]
==== REQ-EMG-144

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall verify each machine in verify mode against a pre-provisioned pinned Apalache without a download at run time.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-041 and ADR-EMG-044. quint verify uses Apalache 0.62.4, provisioned beforehand under QUINT_HOME, offline, and needs Java 21 or later. If the pinned Apalache or Java is missing, <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGQUINT,engquint>> exits 2 with the missing item and does not fetch it. quint verify reports a deadlock as a violation, so verify runs with the Apalache option no-deadlock. Owner statement of 2026-11-12 (verbatim): "all the tools are approved use them in CI even if you cannot install them here now." The pins (quint npm 0.33.1, Apalache 0.62.4 tarball sha256 8ac8488422c30d552735bae11b92a2d014d8e02e8608702acc08f9a2d8a9abb2, Temurin JDK 21) were chosen by the implementing agent and await the owner confirmation.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_145]]
==== REQ-EMG-145

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall record each Quint result with the sha256 of its module so that a stale result is no <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>>.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-041 and ADR-EMG-042. The results file holds, per machine and invariant, the verdict, the sha256 of the .qnt it was produced from, the quint version, backend, mode (run or verify), the bounds (max-steps, max-samples) and the seed. A result whose sha256 differs from the committed module is stale: it is never <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>>, and check warns with the machine and invariant.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_146]]
==== REQ-EMG-146

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall count a passing non-stale formal result as <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ANALYSIS,analysis>> <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>> for the linked <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> in the trace matrix.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-042. <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGQUINT,engquint>> check writes a sha-verified result into test-results/ with kind formal; internal/trace and the codescan inferred verification read it. A pass whose sha256 matches the module is <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ANALYSIS,analysis>> <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>> for each REQ-* the invariant is linked to; a stale result is not <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_EVIDENCE,evidence>>, and a failed result is recorded as failed, so the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> is failed and never unverified (ADR-EMG-045 item 20). The tier policy and the verification status roll-up treat it like any other verification entry. A result is current only if the named module is a generated Quint module of that machine inside the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> root (ADR-EMG-045 items 42 to 44).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_147]]
==== REQ-EMG-147

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall write a requirement-keyed formal entry for each Quint result into the Gemara evaluation log.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-042. Entries are keyed by <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>, so no requirement-to-control mapping is needed: a passing non-stale result is a passed entry, a failed result a failed one and a stale result a not-run one with the reason.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_148]]
==== REQ-EMG-148

While <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FEAT_MCP_SERVER,mcp server is enabled>>, when <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MCP_TOOL_CALL_RECEIVED,mcp tool call is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report requirement-level formal results in the verification tools.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-042. MCP verification.status and verification.gaps gain a requirement-level formal result of pass, failed or stale; <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.authoringContract documents the machines block (fieldSets for machine, variable, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_STATE,state>>, transition and invariant, the expression operator table, the machine diagnostics and their tier rows).

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_149]]
==== REQ-EMG-149

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall keep the generated Quint modules with the other generated artifacts and report any drift in the <<REF_IDX-MACHINE_SM_ARTIFACT_FRESHNESS,artifact freshness>> gate.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-040 and ADR-EMG-043. The modules under generated/quint/ (hard-coded in the scripts) are regenerated by scripts/validate-all.sh; the freshness gate compares the hashes before and after, so a <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_MODEL_CHANGE,model change>> without regenerated modules fails. This is the mvp-tier Quint <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_150]]
==== REQ-EMG-150

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_CODE_HEALTH,code health>> smells for each function of Go, Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript and Python source files.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-046, ADR-EMG-047. The named codes are health.complex_method, health.large_method, health.deep_nesting, health.bumpy_road, health.complex_conditional, health.excess_arguments, health.primitive_obsession, health.brain_method, health.large_assertion_block and health.duplicated_assertion_block. Thresholds, decision points and assertion statements per language are in ADR-EMG-047. A smell that cannot be computed for a language (primitive_obsession needs known types, so never for JavaScript) is reported as unsupported for that language and never as a silent zero. Anonymous closures count toward their enclosing function. The <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ANALYSIS,analysis>> is our own and is not CodeScene <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_CODE_HEALTH,Code Health>>.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_151]]
==== REQ-EMG-151

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall compute an explainable <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_CODE_HEALTH,code health>> score from 1.0 to 10.0 for each source file.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-048. The score starts at 10.0 and each smell deducts its weight times a severity factor (warn 1, high 2); per-function deductions combine with diminishing returns (worst counts fully, next times 0.5, the rest times 0.25 with the whole tail counted at most 2.0 points, ADR-EMG-059); the result is clamped to 1.0..10.0 with one decimal. Bands: green at 8.0 or above, yellow at 4.0 or above, red below 4.0 (OWNER). The weights table is versioned (scoringVersion 2 since the capped tail; an imported report of version 1 or 2 is read as it is) and published in the report. Test files are scored separately and are excluded from production roll-ups by default. The score is our own and is never presented as a CodeScene score.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_152]]
==== REQ-EMG-152

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall roll up file <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_CODE_HEALTH,code health>> scores along the traceability of the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-049. A <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_FUNCTIONAL_UNIT,functional unit>> is the LOC-weighted mean of its files plus its worst file, attributed by the file-level ENGMODEL-OWNER-UNIT marker (one value per file). A <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> is reached through the TRLC-LINKS of marker-linked symbols (Symbol.Implements), joined to functions by path and line range, and reports its findings and the worst score of the files of those functions (a function has no score of its own). The project roll-up is the LOC-weighted mean, the worst performer and the count per band.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_153]]
==== REQ-EMG-153

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall validate the manifest health block including exclude, thresholds, overrides and waivers.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-051. The health block is optional below product and required at product and operational (<<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_165,REQ-EMG-165>>). exclude uses the dialect of inferenceHints.exclude (path.Match per segment, only a trailing /**), not gitignore semantics. thresholds name known codes with warn and high values that are ordered; overrides apply thresholds by path; a waiver is {code, path, function, decision}. Unknown keys and malformed shapes are rejected by the CUE contract and the loader; unknown codes, unordered thresholds and exclude patterns outside the dialect are the errors <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.invalid_health_exclude, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.invalid_health_threshold, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.invalid_health_override and <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.invalid_health_waiver of <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_VALIDATION,validation>>, each naming the field.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_154]]
==== REQ-EMG-154

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall require each <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_CODE_HEALTH,code health>> waiver to cite an existing accepted decision.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-051 and ADR-EMG-052. health.waiver_unjustified is an error at every tier and is untiered: the cited decision is missing or its status is not accepted (the acceptance reference check of the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> is reused). health.waiver_unused follows the debt row (a warning up to mvp, an error from product): the waiver matches no finding, so it can be removed. A waiver whose decision is not accepted waives nothing in scan and check. A waiver suppresses one code for one function in one file and is listed in the report as waived, never silently dropped.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_155]]
==== REQ-EMG-155

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_CODE_HEALTH,code health>> findings in <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGHEALTH,enghealth>> reports with the severity of the project life-cycle tier.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-052 (OWNER decision). Debt findings (every health smell code) are warnings up to mvp and errors at product and operational, the row WWWEE (WWEEE with the safety bundle; ADR-EMG-057). health.regression, a new or worsened high finding against the base revision, is keyed in TierPolicy with the row WWWEE: a warning below product, an error from product, and from mvp with the safety bundle (row WWEEE). health.waiver_unjustified is an untiered error and health.waiver_unused follows the debt row. lifecycle.raise with health.* stays the owner escape hatch that makes debt blocking at a lower tier. Smell findings, regressions, unused waivers and stale baseline entries exist only in <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGHEALTH,enghealth>> reports (internal/health imports internal/validate, so <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_VALIDATION,validation>> cannot emit them); <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_VALIDATION,validation>> reports only the configuration and waiver diagnostics of the health block.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_156]]
==== REQ-EMG-156

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall classify each <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_CODE_HEALTH,code health>> finding against a base revision of the working tree.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-053. Findings are keyed by (path, qualified name, code). The base file is read with git show as raw bytes, never a checkout; renames come from git diff -M --name-status, and a renamed function with the same body hash is not new. New means absent at base; worsened means the metric grew past a higher severity or by at least 20 percent; otherwise existing. Existing debt never fails <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGHEALTH,enghealth>> check (<<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGHEALTH,enghealth>> scan --fail-on-error does fail on an error finding that is neither waived nor baselined). In an empty repository (no base commit) every finding is new and the check warns. In a shallow clone whose base revision is missing the check fails with a setup error (exit 2), because a silent pass would hide regressions.

What this diagram shows: this requirement-to-unit mapping extended with inferred runtime/code plus verification evidence attached to each requirement and unit.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_157]]
==== REQ-EMG-157

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall write the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_CODE_HEALTH,code health>> report in the neutral format engmod-health/1.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-050. The report is also exported as SARIF 2.1.0, and the roll-up of the unit, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> and project levels is ADR-EMG-049. The HealthReport JSON carries the schema string engmod-health/1 and is described by a published JSON Schema document that a test validates reports against. The SARIF 2.1.0 export is new code with no precedent in the repository. A report that conforms to engmod-health/1 can be imported in place of the built-in <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ANALYSIS,analysis>>: this is the seam for another engine behind an Engine <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_INTERFACE,interface>>. There is no CodeScene adapter.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_158]]
==== REQ-EMG-158

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall run <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_CODE_HEALTH,code health>> <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ANALYSIS,analysis>> with <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGHEALTH,enghealth>> scan, check and baseline, exiting 0 when ok, 1 on blocking findings and 2 on a setup error.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-046, ADR-EMG-052 and ADR-EMG-053. cmd/<<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGHEALTH,enghealth>> has the subcommands scan (report and roll-ups; it exits 1 only with --fail-on-error and an error finding that is neither waived nor baselined), baseline (write and --check the committed baseline) and check (delta between a base revision and the working tree, with the blocking decision of the tier policy). A setup error (unreadable <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>, missing base revision, unreadable or non-conforming imported report, a path outside the repository) exits 2 and never counts as a pass.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_159]]
==== REQ-EMG-159

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall cache the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_CODE_HEALTH,code health>> result of each file by content hash and produce deterministic output.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-054. The cache lives under .engmod/cache/health, keyed by the sha256 of the file content, the language, the thresholds and scoringVersion; a changed key is a miss. Output is sorted, and a committed report holds no timestamps and no absolute paths. The cache key also holds the path, the engine name and version and a key-layout version. The cache is used by check and by scan (--no-cache turns it off), it is off by default when CI is set, and it is refused when files under .engmod are tracked by git (an unprotected cache entry could hide a finding). Target: a check of one changed file under 1 s when warm (measured 0.2 to 0.4 s in docs/code-health-dogfood.md).

What this diagram shows: this requirement-to-unit mapping extended with inferred runtime/code plus verification evidence attached to each requirement and unit.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_160]]
==== REQ-EMG-160

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall produce byte-identical <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_VALIDATION_DIAGNOSTIC,validation diagnostics>> and generated documents for a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> without a health block at the tiers below product.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-046 and ADR-EMG-052, narrowed by ADR-EMG-066. <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_FU_CODE_HEALTH,Code health>> is opt-in through the manifest health block below product; at product and operational the block is required (<<REF_IDX-REQ_REQ_EMG_165,REQ-EMG-165>>) and its absence is the error health.block_missing. Below product and without the block, <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_VALIDATION,validation>> reports no health.* diagnostic and the generated documents carry no health section; the tier policy table and the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_AUTHORING,authoring>> contract are the same for every <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_161]]
==== REQ-EMG-161

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_GENERATION_RUN_REQUESTED,generation run is requested>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall treat a finding listed in the committed health baseline as accepted debt.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-059. The manifest health.baseline names a file and an accepted decision. A finding in the file, matched by path, qualified function name and code, is reported as baselined: it counts toward the score and is neither an error nor counted by --fail-on-error. A baseline entry that matches no finding is health.baseline_stale (a warning below operational, an error at operational), so the baseline can only shrink. health.baseline_unreadable is an untiered error for a missing or malformed file. A new or worsened high finding (health.regression) is never baselined. <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_ENGHEALTH,enghealth>> baseline write creates the file and --check verifies it.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_162]]
==== REQ-EMG-162

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report the error lifecycle.missing for a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> without a lifecycle block.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-061 and ADR-EMG-066. lifecycle.missing is a rank-0 code: no tier, raise entry or POA&M defers entry changes it. The library functions that load a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> stay lenient so that embedding tools can report; <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_VALIDATION,validation>> and every command line tool error. Remedy: run the ef-tier-up skill.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_163]]
==== REQ-EMG-163

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report an error when the lifecycle has no bundles, no tier decision, or a tier decision without a Bundles line.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-061 and ADR-EMG-066. lifecycle.bundles_missing, lifecycle.tier_decision_missing and lifecycle.tier_decision_mismatch. The default of Foundation for a missing Bundles line is removed. Each error carries the remedy of the ef-tier-up skill.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_164]]
==== REQ-EMG-164

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report an error when requirementLinks or lintRun.mode is missing, <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_INVALID,invalid>> or guided at mvp or above.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-061 and ADR-EMG-066. <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.requirement_links_missing, lint.mode_missing, lint.mode_invalid and lint.mode_guided_at_tier. Guided is allowed only below mvp. The mode is read case-insensitively.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_166]]
==== REQ-EMG-166

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>>.unsupported_schema_version with a remedy for a missing or unsupported schemaVersion.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-061 and ADR-EMG-066. The loader error and the diagnostic both carry the remedy: set schemaVersion 2 at the top of the file (an upgrade command is planned in engineering-flow and is not named until it exists). The loader checks schemaVersion in Go before the CUE contract for every document type, so a missing version and a version other than 2 get the remedy, not a CUE conflict message.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_169]]
==== REQ-EMG-169

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall keep a remedy for every required-switch code in one table that an inventory test compares with the codes in both directions.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-061 and ADR-EMG-066. TestRequiredSwitchesHaveRemedies triggers each required code from a complete bundle with one switch removed and compares the codes with the remedy table in both directions.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_170]]
==== REQ-EMG-170

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report a source file whose owner unit marker is missing or names no <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_FUNCTIONAL_UNIT,functional unit>>.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-069. code.owner_unresolved is reported once per file, row WWWEE. Test files, generated files (a Code generated header or an at-generated tag in the first 10 lines) and files owned by an alias are left out. The remedy names the ef-code-linking skill.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_171]]
==== REQ-EMG-171

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> link marker that names a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> or a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_CATALOG,catalog>> term instead of a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> element.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-069. code.model_link_kind_mismatch, row WWWEE. KnownModelIDs stays as it is and a second <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_VIEW,view>> maps each identifier to its kind. A <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> belongs in the trace link marker of the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>>, not in the <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> link marker.

[[REF_REQ_REQ_EMG_172]]
==== REQ-EMG-172

When <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_EVT_MODEL_UPDATED,model updated event is received>>, the <<REF_IDX-CATALOG_SYS_ENGINEERING_MODEL_GO,engineering model go>> shall report an event-driven or state-driven <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> that no machine invariant or applies-to element models.


NOTE: ADR-EMG-069. behavior.requirement_unmodeled, row DDWWE. The <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirement>> pattern comes from the EARS lint. Only a <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_MODEL,model>> that declares at least one machine is asked, and retired, rejected and derived <<REF_IDX-ENGMODEL_TERM_REQUIREMENT,requirements>> are exempt.
